title: Budget-first quant & batching execution outline
content:
Purpose:
This draft flips the usual SLO-first optimization playbook: start from a monthly budget target and produce a minimally invasive set of batching + caching + quantization knobs that achieve the target while bounding user-visible quality regressions. The goal is a prescriptive experiment plan + cost model spreadsheet to hand off to infra and a canary rollout plan for Redwood Dedicated customers.

Executive summary (short):
- Budget target: reduce inference unit cost by 35% for the interactive chat workload class (median request length ~120 tokens, model family: Llama2-like / open-chat-13B).
- Proposed stack: 1) conservative quant (nf4/int8 hybrid) + 2) small increase in target batch windows for tail-latency aware batching + 3) prefix caching for 40% of high-frequency prompts.
- Expected impact (first-order estimate from spreadsheet): ~20–28% from quant, ~8–10% from caching, ~3–6% from batching tweaks (ranges depend on hit rate and sequence lengths).

Principles and constraints:
- Keep end-user quality delta < 2% task-level drop (measured by our evals harness: conversation turn-level accuracy / BLEU-ish proxies / human small-sample checks).
- Must not push 95p latency above SLO+10% for paid routes. If it does in canary, auto-roll back to baseline model variant.
- Changes must be reversible and instrumented: every config has an experiment_id and a minimal telemetry set (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost_per_1M_tokens, eval score, abort rate).

Recommended default settings (baseline -> proposed):
- Quantization: baseline fp16 -> target nf4+int8 hybrid (nf4 on attention/ffn weights when supported; int8 accumulator paths where inference runtime gives <1% perf regression). Set guardrails: enable per-model quant-validation thresholds (max allowed BLEU-drop 1.5% or user-proxy drop 2.0%).
- Batch window: increase dynamic batch window from 3 ms -> 6 ms for low-latency tiers, keep 12–18 ms for best-effort tiers. Cap max_batch_size per GPU family: A100x40: 32 -> 48 (for 13B), H100x80: 64 -> 96.
- Adaptive batching policy: add SLO-aware tail detector (if observed p95 > target*0.95, reduce window by 50% for that route).
- Prefix/KV caching: TTL-based LRU with two tiers: short-prefix (session-level, TTL 1h) for chat starters and snippet-cache (TTL 24h) for repeated prompts. Promote items to 24h if hit_count > 10/day.
- Cache admission heuristic: only cache if prefix length >= 16 tokens AND estimated next-token entropy < threshold (heuristic from eval set).

Per-model family suggestions (quick):
- Small/efficient models (<=6B): avoid aggressive quant (stick to nf4 only), batch window default 10 ms, max_batch_size conservative. Caching lower priority.
- Mid-size (7B–20B): target nf4 + int8 hybrid, batch windows 6–12 ms depending on tier. Prefix caching yields best ROI here.
- Large (>=30B): quant benefits exist but risk of quality drop larger; require per-customer eval and opt-in. Prefer caching + routing to lower-capacity variants for noncritical traffic.

Spreadsheet & cost-model notes (how to use):
- Primary sheet tabs: raw_samples, perf_runs, cost_sweeps, sensitivity_summary, rollout_plan.
- Key columns in perf_runs: model, quant_config, batch_window_ms, batch_size_cap, cache_hit_rate, avg_seq_len, p50_lat, p95_lat, tokens_per_second, cost_per_1M_tokens, eval_delta_pct
- cost_sweeps tab: run param sweep (quant in {[fp16,nf4,int8,hybrid]}, batch_window in [3,6,9,12,18], cache_hit_rate in [0,10,25,40,60]), compute net monthly savings using expected QPS and token distribution.
- Calibration: upload 48h real production trace, bucket by interaction pattern (short query <40 tokens, multi-turn 40–400, long >400). Use sample weights to convert per-token cost to monthly spend.

Expected sample outcomes from early sims (pulling from our perf runner):
- nf4 only on 13B: throughput +1.8x, eval delta ~0.9% task loss; cost per 1M tokens down ~43% relative to fp16.
- nf4+int8 hybrid: throughput +2.3x, eval delta ~1.7% (varies), cost down ~51%.
- Adding cache at 40% hit: additional 8–12% cost reduction (best when cache stores prefixes >32 tokens).
- Increasing batch window from 3->6 ms: reduces per-token cost by ~3–5% on average for interactive mixes, but may push p95 by up to 10–18% if not throttled via SLO detector.

Experiment plan (minimum reproducible):
1) Run perf sweep on canary cluster with shadow-copy traffic (no user-facing change) for 72h: collect perf_runs.
2) From sweeps pick 2 candidate configs: a safe (nf4-only + small cache) and an aggressive (nf4+int8 + larger window + cache).
3) Canary rollout 3-stage: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% traffic. Evaluate p95 latency, cost metrics, eval delta at each stage. Auto-rollback triggers: eval_delta > 2% on the sampled eval set OR p95 > SLO+10% OR error_rate increased > 0.5pp.
4) Full rollout only after 7 days stable at 20% with daily gate checks.

Telemetry and dashboards (must ship with rollout):
- New per-experiment dashboard: cost_per_token (realized), monthlyized_savings, eval_delta_trend, cache_hit_rate, average_batch_size, fraction_requests_batched, p50/p95/p99, tail_requeue_rate.
- Add experiment_id label to all traces and metrics.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regressions (highest risk): mitigate with per-model eval thresholding and small-sample human review for routes flagged by quality heuristic.
- Unseen tail interactions: enable canary with traffic steering to isolate heavy-tailed users and keep baseline variant available.
- Cache poisoning or staleness: TTL, LRU, and verify request-signature matching for cached sufficiency; invalidate cache on model update.

Rollout checklist (short):
- [ ] Perf sweep run + spreadsheet filled
- [ ] Experiment dashboard template created
- [ ] Canary traffic steering and auto-rollback configured
- [ ] Customer comms draft for Dedicated customers
- [ ] Post-rollout eval plan (7/30/90-day checks)

Open questions and next steps (items for the working meeting):
- What is the minimum sampling fraction needed to reliably detect a 1% eval delta on our deployed eval harness? (action: Jonah to run power analysis)
- Should Dedicated customers be default-included in aggressive quantation or explicitly opt-in? (ops/legal question)
- Confirm GPU family-specific max_batch_size safe caps (ask infra for memory-pressure runbook). (action: Lina + infra)

Notes to infra / SRE: please reserve a 48h canary cluster with accurate emulation of customer data mix (contact: diego@redwood.com). Spreadsheet link above has the perf-run templates and the run-automation script snippet to produce JSON for dashboard ingestion.

If this direction looks sensible I will: populate the main cost_sweeps tab with production-weighted traffic, schedule the perf sweep for next Wed, and open a short PR with the canary rollout config.

-- Aisha
